composio.note: Composio lists Todoist as managed OAuth. A separate Todoist MCP toolkit requires your own OAuth app.

need_own_app.answer: Not for prototypes, since Composio provides a managed Todoist app. For launch, use your own app if you want your brand on the consent screen, custom scopes, or a dedicated quota.
reasons: Consent screen shows your app name instead of Composio
Dedicated quota instead of quota shared across Composio users
Shorter trigger polling than the 15-minute managed minimum
Todoist MCP toolkit requires your own app

prerequisites.title: Verified Todoist account
prerequisites.detail: Check you have a verified Todoist user account before starting.

prerequisites.title: Pro account may help
prerequisites.detail: A Pro account may be needed for development; Todoist says it can help if you lack one.

prerequisites.title: HTTPS redirect URLs
prerequisites.detail: Redirect URIs must be HTTPS, though localhost is allowed for testing.

steps.title: Create app in App Management Console
steps.detail: Register your application and add one or more valid OAuth2 redirect URLs. You then get a Client ID and Client Secret.
steps.done_when: You have a Client ID and Client Secret.

steps.title: Copy Composio redirect URI
steps.detail: Copy the redirect URI from the Composio dashboard and check that it is HTTPS before adding it to the Todoist app.
steps.done_when: Redirect URI is saved in the Todoist app.

steps.title: Create Composio auth config
steps.detail: Create the auth config through Composio's API with your own client ID and secret, and set the scopes you need.

steps.title: Connect a test user
steps.detail: Complete the OAuth flow with a test account and confirm the token works.

steps.title: Prepare certification materials
steps.detail: Draft the English description, the not-affiliated statement, and the icon and screenshot specs.
steps.done_when: Form content is ready for submission.

steps.title: Record demo and submit form
steps.detail: Record the demo video and submit the certification form yourself.

steps.title: Wait for certification review
steps.detail: Todoist aims to respond within ten business days and to reply to emails within two.

traps.title: Dynamically registered clients get a client_secret_expires_at value of 0
traps.detail: Dynamically registered clients get a client_secret_expires_at value of 0, meaning their client secrets do not expire.

traps.title: Unpublished token cap
traps.detail: Authorization fails with invalid_application_status if your app exceeds its maximum token limit or is suspended for abuse. The limit is not documented.

traps.title: Naming and disclaimer rules
traps.detail: Todoist cannot be the primary name of your app. The description must say it is not created by, affiliated with, or supported by Todoist.

traps.title: Multiple redirect URIs
traps.detail: If your app has several redirect URIs, redirect_uri is required or the request is rejected with invalid_request. An unconfigured URI also returns an error.

traps.title: Composio consent screen
traps.detail: With the managed app, users see Composio wants to access your account instead of your brand.

traps.title: Certification content rules
traps.detail: The privacy policy must promise not to sell or share user data without consent. All form fields must be in English and all links HTTPS.

traps.title: Zapier-only integrations rejected
traps.detail: Listings are not hosted for services that integrate solely via third-party automation providers or email forwarding.

blockers.what_it_means: The app exceeded the maximum token limit or was suspended for abuse.
blockers.what_to_do: Contact Todoist support; the limit is not published.

blockers.what_it_means: A requested scope is unknown or restricted to first-party use.

evidence.answer: Dynamic client registration is done by POSTing JSON to the Todoist registration endpoint.

evidence.answer: Dynamically registered clients get a client_secret_expires_at value of 0, meaning their client secrets do not expire.

evidence.answer: Clients can use the OAuth Client ID Metadata Document flow instead of a client secret.

evidence.question: G4

evidence.answer: The task:add scope lets an app add new tasks only; the app cannot read or modify existing data.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: Grants read-only access to application data, including tasks, projects, labels, and filters.
evidence.answer: The data:read scope gives read-only access to tasks, projects, labels, and filters.

evidence.question: G4

evidence.answer: The data:read_write scope gives read and write access to tasks, projects, labels, and filters.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: This scope includes task:add and data:read scopes.
evidence.answer: The data:read_write scope includes the task:add and data:read scopes.

evidence.question: G4

evidence.answer: The data:delete scope allows deleting tasks, labels, and filters.

evidence.question: G4

evidence.answer: The project:delete scope allows deleting projects.

evidence.question: G4

evidence.answer: Downloading a backup still requires the data:read_write scope.

evidence.answer: For dynamic client registration, restricted scopes are rejected and the default scope is data:read_write when none is given.

evidence.question: G4

evidence.question: G7

evidence.question: G8

evidence.answer: To activate webhooks for personal use, the developer completes the OAuth process with their own account.

evidence.question: G9

evidence.question: G9

evidence.answer: Client ID Metadata Document redirect URIs must be a non-empty array and must use HTTPS (localhost allowed for testing).

evidence.answer: Registration fails with invalid_client_metadata if a field fails validation, such as a malformed or non-HTTPS redirect URI.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: For security reasons, Todoist only allows webhook urls that have HTTPS enabled and no ports specified in the url.
evidence.answer: Todoist only allows webhook URLs that have HTTPS enabled and no ports specified.

evidence.answer: A registered Todoist application is assigned a unique Client ID and Client Secret, which are needed for the OAuth2 flow.
